after: ## What the syllabus says about Exercise 6
alt: Side by side: Exercise 5 is 8 marks for about 120 words of functional writing from prompts or pictures; Exercise 6 is 16 marks, just over a quarter of the paper, for about 200 words of continuous prose from short prompts. The difference is development.
caption: Twice the marks for developed, linked ideas, not just more words.

alt: A table of five formats with their Urdu names, conventions and usual register: article (مضمون), blog post (بلاگ), report (رپورٹ), review (تبصرہ) and letter (خط). A report needs a title, a purpose statement and recommendations (سفارشات).
caption: Each format has conventions; showing them earns W5.

after: ## Reading the task: purpose, format, audience
alt: A table of rubric verbs and the language each calls for: بیان کیجیے (describe), وضاحت کیجیے (explain: کیونکہ), اپنی رائے دیجیے (opinion: میرے خیال میں), مشورہ دیجیے (advise: چاہیے) and قائل کیجیے (persuade). For a formal reader, prefer مدعو کرنا to بلانا and تقریب to فنکشن.
caption: Match your language to the verb in the rubric and the register to the reader.

alt: The prompt کچھ پروگرام بہت لمبے تھے۔ is copied almost unchanged in the undeveloped version, while the developed version names the three-hour speech contest and adds a consequence with جس کی وجہ سے: younger pupils became restless and many people left before the prizes.
caption: Name something specific, then say what followed from it.

after: ## Planning about 200 words in about 30 minutes
alt: A 30-minute plan of 3 minutes planning, 22 writing and 5 checking, and a four-paragraph shape: an introduction of about 30 words, two developed main points of about 60-70 words each, and a conclusion of about 30-40 words.
caption: Two developed middle paragraphs carry most of the 200 words.

alt: A table of Urdu linking devices by function: adding (اس کے علاوہ، مزید یہ کہ), contrasting (لیکن، تاہم، دوسری طرف), cause and result (کیونکہ، اس لیے، چنانچہ), sequencing (سب سے پہلے، پھر، آخر میں) and concluding (مختصر یہ کہ).
caption: A range of linking words, not the same one every time, shows W2.

alt: Five Urdu structures with glosses: a condition with اگر… تو, a relative clause with جو, a passive, a suggestion with میری تجویز ہے کہ, and a comparison with کے مقابلے میں. Below, the Urdu full stop, comma and question mark, and spellings such as ضروری (not ظروری) and ذریعے (not زریعے).
caption: Plan a few structures in deliberately, then check punctuation and spelling.
